newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Capstone aims to set up branch in HK.
newsitem.headline: Capstone aims to set up branch in HK.

text.p: Appliance parts maker Shenzhen Capstone Industrial Co Ltd plans to set up a branch in Hong Kong to improve exports, the company said on Thursday.
Capstone will submit an application to establish the branch to the authorities in Beijing in the near future, a company spokesman told the China Securities Bulletin.
The branch would be responsible for importing raw materials for Capstone and marketing its products abroad, he said.
Nearly 80 percent of Capstone's core product, electrolytic capacitors, are exported to Japan and Southeast Asia, with the remaining 20 percent sold in mainland China, he said.
Capstone's exports are currently conducted through its biggest shareholder, Hong Kong-based Firstone International Holdings Ltd, which also acts as a raw materials buyer for Capstone, he said.
According to Capstone's 1996 interim report, Firstone held 25.38 million founder shares in Capstone as of June 30 this year, accounting for 37.11 percent of its total share capital.

Capstone was set up by Firstone in 1988 as a Hong Kong-invested enterprise in Shenzhen. It was restructured into a joint stock entity in 1990 and listed on the South China bourse in 1993, according to the spokesman.

He said Capstone expects to wait a long time to receive approval from Beijing for a branch in Hong Kong, because it was much harder to get approval for a branch in Hong Kong than elsewhere. He did not elaborate.

Capstone said in its interim report that under Chinese accounting standards it had unaudited net earnings of 4.26 million yuan in the first half of 1996, down from 9.11 million in the same period the previous year.
